about: Personal and household belongings for generation-2 houses (docs/design/TIER1_SWEEP.md section 14.4), read by house_sim/generator/belongings.py. Items are listed in placement order (outerwear and bags before the small things that can sit in their pockets). Probabilities are per resident of the role (or per household); the first type of 'types' that the registry knows is used, and an item whose types are all missing is skipped and reported as a layout-audit note (the owner domain adds the type).

spots.doc: A spot is AREA.WHAT. AREA: own (the owner's bedroom), entry (first entryway, else mudroom), kitchen, living, office, dining, coat_closet, master (the primary bedroom). WHAT: a type name (nightstand, dresser, desk, counter, side_table, coffee_table, bench, sofa, bed, shoe_rack, key_hook, coat_hooks, closet_rod, key_bowl, umbrella_stand), or closet (built-in closet or wardrobe), table (kitchen or dining table), floor, junk_drawer, top_drawer (a dresser's top drawer), filing_cabinet, coat_pocket (a pocket of the owner's outerwear), bag (the owner's bag or backpack). Hooks and rods hang the item, containers take it inside, surfaces carry it, floor puts it on the floor where it cuts no walking route.
spots.alt: [spot, weight] or [spot, weight, period]: where the item ends up when the owner left it out of place (period day or night limits the alternative to that time).

displacement.doc: P(an item with alternatives is away from its home) = base + untidy x (1 - tidiness) (sweep 14.4). Assumption: about 1 in 5 everyday items is out of place for an average household; a very tidy person still mislays 1 in 20.
